{"id":"persona-5s4b.107","title":"jsonwebtoken 9 has CVE-2026-25537 type confusion leading to authorization bypass","description":"Dependabot flagged this on first push to GitHub.

CVE-2026-25537 — jsonwebtoken < 10.3.0, type confusion that leads to potential
authorization bypass. Patched in 10.3.0. Workspace Cargo.toml:47 pins
jsonwebtoken = "9".

Why this is S0 here rather than a routine bump: jsonwebtoken is the library that
signs every JWT-SVID (persona-core/src/signer.rs) and performs the only signature
verification the daemon does (persona-grpc/src/service.rs ValidateJWTSVID). An
authorization-bypass class defect in that library sits directly under the whole
credential model. It compounds the existing S0 band rather than being independent
of it: .82 already notes ValidateJWTSVID verifies against the local ephemeral key
only, and .30 that OIDC input is never verified at all.

Caveat for whoever takes this: 9 -> 10.3.0 is a major version bump and is likely
to be a breaking API change, not a patch bump. Check Algorithm/Validation/
EncodingKey signatures before assuming a version bump is sufficient. Verify the
advisory's exploitability against how signer.rs and service.rs actually call the
API — type confusion may or may not be reachable through these call paths.

This also empirically confirms .31 (no dependency vulnerability audit in CI or
Makefile): a cargo-audit or cargo-deny step would have caught this before push.
GitHub caught it only because the repo went public.
